haiku-low.q1: They see the same generic 200 message as a real account. Nothing is stored and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: They get the same generic 200 response, but no row is stored and no email is queued. The existing links stay valid.
haiku-low.q3: It expires 30 minutes after creation. Being used, or a newer link being issued for the account, ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link is untouched and still usable. Length and breach checks run before consuming, so the user can retry until expiry.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions are deleted, including this device's, so it is logged out on its next request. Redirected to login; user signs in again.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told and gets no email; they must request again.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and put into the queued job's link. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and selects the reset_tokens row where consumed_at is NULL and expires_at is in the future. Read only.
haiku-low.q9: Not in a separate counter: it counts the user's reset_tokens rows created in the last hour. Old rows age out of the window; rows are not deleted on consume.
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction as the insert, before commit, all of the account's unconsumed earlier links get consumed_at set to now.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: consume the token, update password_hash, delete all sessions. The confirmation email is queued only after commit.
haiku-low.q12: An atomic UPDATE sets consumed_at only where it is still NULL and returns a row; the losing submit gets zero rows and sees 'expired'.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic 200: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent, and no row or job is created.
sonnet.q2: The 4th request within an hour (count >= 3) gets the same generic 200, with no new row and no job. No new link is sent and the old link stays.
sonnet.q3: A link works for 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if it is consumed by a successful reset, or if a newer link is issued (which sets consumed_at on older ones).
sonnet.q4: The link is untouched and still usable. The server returns 422 and the user can retry until the link expires.
sonnet.q5: No devices stay logged in, because all of the user's sessions are deleted, including the resetting device. They are logged out on their next request. The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in with the new password, since no session is created.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told. They must request again, and the failed attempt still counts toward their 3 per hour.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the raw token (32 random bytes) at request time, stores only its SHA-256 hash, and puts the raw token in the link in the queue job payload ({user, link with raw token}). The worker sends that job through the mail provider.
sonnet.q8: The server selects from reset_tokens WHERE token_hash = sha256(RAW) AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). This is read-only and burns nothing. A matching row means valid. No row (invalid, expired, used or unknown) shows the "link has expired" page.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. The count comes from reset_tokens rows with created_at > now() - 1 hour. Old requests drop out as their created_at passes the one-hour window. Rows are not deleted at consume time, and any cleanup must keep rows for at least an hour.
sonnet.q10: When the count is under 3 and before inserting the new row, an UPDATE sets consumed_at = now() on all of the user's reset_tokens where consumed_at IS NULL. This runs in the same transaction as the insert, after the FOR UPDATE lock on the user row, and kills the old links.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token is marked consumed (UPDATE ... RETURNING user_id), users.password_hash is updated, and all of the user's sessions are deleted. The "your password was changed" email is enqueued after COMMIT, as a separate step.
sonnet.q12: The atomic UPDATE reset_tokens SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token_hash = ... AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING user_id. Only one gets a row, and the loser gets 0 rows, rolls back and sees the "expired" page.
